8154.question_text: The appearance of Moses and Elijah at the transfiguration underscores the importance in the ministry of Jesus of
8154.explanation: The appearance of Moses and Elijah at the transfiguration underscores the importance of "the law and the prophets" in the ministry of Jesus. This event is described in the Gospels of Matthew (Matthew 17:1-13), Mark (Mark 9:2-13), and Luke (Luke 9:28-36). Moses represents the Law, and Elijah represents the Prophets. Their presence emphasizes the continuity of Jesus' ministry with the Old Testament Scriptures and the fulfilment of the prophetic expectations regarding the Messiah.

8175.explanation:
According to Luke 4:1–13 (RSV), the second temptation is when the devil shows Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and offers them to Him in exchange for worship.

Order of Temptations in Luke’s Gospel:

  1. Turn stone into bread – Luke 4:3

  2. Worship Satan in exchange for worldly kingdoms – Luke 4:5–7 ✅

  3. Throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple – Luke 4:9–11

“And the devil took him up, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time, and said to him, ‘To you I will give all this authority and their glory; for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whom I will. If you, then, will worship me, it shall all be yours.’”

8253.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
8253.question_text: According to Psalm 51, the sacrifice acceptable to God is
8253.explanation:
In Psalm 51:17, King David writes:

"The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise."

This passage emphasises that humility and repentance are more important to God than ritual sacrifices. While sacrifices (like lambs without blemish) were part of the religious practices in the Old Testament, what God truly desires is a genuine, repentant heart—a broken spirit and contrite heart.
